subproblems.title: A set of finite H⁰-measure is countably 0-rectifiable (parent step 0, case n = 0)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and M ⊆ ℝ^P (no measurability assumed) with H⁰(M) < ∞, where H⁰ = μHE[0]. Then M is countably 0-rectifiable in the sense of SimonGMT (CountablyRectifiable 0 M): there are an H⁰-null set M₀ and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ⁰).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), μHE[0] M ≠ ∞ → CountablyRectifiable 0 M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cbrr_rectifiable_dim_zero (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.rectifiable-a1.dim_zero-a1, status accepted, candidate 7507e179db81e9b0fe5fcab34c07a83f97e11e68), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. It is the case n = 0 of step 1 of the selected node's supplied proof ("n = 0 (M finite, constant maps)"). The numbered proof below is that node's accepted natural-language proof, copied verbatim except for one added parenthesis in step 3.
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 109–111) and its proof "⇐" (lines 145–274), where this degenerate case is implicit.

1. H⁰ is the counting measure on points. By Mathlib `MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero`, μHE[0] = μH[0], and by `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton`, μH[0]({x}) = 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
2. M is finite. Suppose M were infinite. Let r ≥ 0 be any real number and k := ⌈r⌉ ∈ ℕ. Since M is infinite it contains a finite set s with exactly k elements (Mathlib `Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq`). Singletons are closed, hence Borel, so by finite additivity μH[0](s) = Σ_{x∈s} μH[0]({x}) = k (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.sum_measure_singleton`). By monotonicity μH[0](M) ≥ μH[0](s) = k ≥ r. As r ≥ 0 was arbitrary, μH[0](M) = ∞, i.e. H⁰(M) = ∞, contradicting the hypothesis H⁰(M) ≠ ∞. Hence M is finite, in particular countable.
3. Points are Lipschitz images of ℝ⁰. For x ∈ ℝ^P the constant map c_x : ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P, u ↦ x, is Lipschitz with constant 0 and has range {x} (ℝ⁰ = {0} is nonempty); therefore {x} is countably 0-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_range`).
4. Countable union. M = ⋃₀ {{x} : x ∈ M}. The family {{x} : x ∈ M} is the image of the countable set M, hence countable, and each member is countably 0-rectifiable by step 3. By SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_sUnion`, M is countably 0-rectifiable. ∎
proof_key_steps: An infinite set contains k-element subsets of measure k for every k, so H⁰(M) < ∞ forces M finite.
Each point is the range of a constant 0-Lipschitz map ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P.
A countable union of countably 0-rectifiable sets is countably 0-rectifiable.

subproblems.title: Lusin–Egorov: uniform lower density and cone bounds on a subset of almost full measure (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 ⇐, (4)–(9))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n], μ := Hⁿ⌞M), and Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces of ℝ^P such that x ↦ p_{Q(x)} (orthogonal projection, an element of L(ℝ^P) with the operator norm) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and M has approximate tangent space Q(x) at μ-a.e. x. Let a, b, ε be real numbers with ofReal(a) < ωₙ = unitBallVolume n, b > 0 and ε > 0. Then there are E ⊆ M and δ > 0 such that Hⁿ(M ∖ E) < ε, dim Q(x) = n for every x ∈ E, and for all x, y ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ: ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ), where X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|}.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cbrr_uniform_density_on_large_set (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.rectifiable-a1.uniform_density-a1, status accepted, candidate 0bc462947c52de7a9c37ba81f905adbee7d845bc), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. It is steps 2–3 of the selected node's supplied proof (densities at tangent points; Lusin and Egorov); the supplied proof's closing note states that this accepted theorem supplies step 3. Part E below reproduces the node's accepted natural-language proof (its frozen handoff text) step by step: the sibling references are renamed to part labels, the steps are relabeled E1–E6, and its source paragraph is condensed into the Source line and the Part E header. It cites three accepted DAG theorems at byte-identical frozen types, which are this node's own resolved dependencies: doragm_approxTangent_lower_density (Part B), cbrr_tangent_cone_density_zero (Part C) and dor_ims_lusin_measurable_continuousOn (Part D). Parts B and C in turn use rsd_cmr_ir_blowUp_image_measure (Part A). So that this proof is self-contained, Parts A–D prove these four lemmas. Part C reproduces the accepted handoff proof of cbrr_tangent_cone_density_zero. Parts A, B and D are the proofs of rsd_cmr_ir_blowUp_image_measure, doragm_approxTangent_lower_density and dor_ims_lusin_measurable_continuousOn that were audited when these theorems were reused in the accepted decomposition of the identically typed node cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent; their own accepted Lean candidates may use different, equivalent arguments. GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean at the candidate commit contains kernel-checked proofs of all four lemmas. It formalizes E1–E5 through four further accepted helpers: cbrr_ud_lusin_of_aestronglyMeasurable, cbrr_ud_isClosed_closedBall_mass_ge, cbrr_ud_isClosed_cone_mass_le and cbrr_ud_uniformize_eventually. The selected proof applies this child with a = (1 − ε₀)ωₙ, b = ε₀ωₙ and ε₀ = 2⁻¹16⁻ⁿ; the statement allows any real a, b, ε with ofReal(a) < ωₙ, b > 0 and ε > 0.
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 91–107) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇐" (lines 145–219): the closed set F of (4), the densities (5)–(6), the functions f_k, q_k and (7), Egoroff's theorem (8) and the uniform bounds (9).
Notation. Hⁿ = μHE[n]; ωₙ = unitBallVolume n = Lⁿ(B₁(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞); η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT `blowUpMap x r`); p_V is the orthogonal projection onto V. "Q is the approximate tangent space of M at x" (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q) means dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|}. In Part C, where one subspace Q and one point x are fixed, X(x) := {z : 2|p_Q(z − x)| < |z − x|} and X := {y : 2|p_Q y| < |y|} is the cone at 0, so X(x) = x + X.

Part A (scaling; accepted theorem rsd_cmr_ir_blowUp_image_measure). For x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and any S ⊆ ℝ^P: Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = ofReal(r⁻ⁿ)·Hⁿ(S).
A1. Factorization. η_{x,r} = h ∘ τ, where τ(y) = y − x and h is the homothety with centre 0 and ratio r⁻¹ ≠ 0; hence η_{x,r}(S) = h(τ(S)).
A2. Translation. τ is an isometry of ℝ^P, so Hⁿ(τ(S)) = Hⁿ(S) (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`).
A3. Homothety. For every T ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(h(T)) = |r⁻¹|ⁿ Hⁿ(T) (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image`, valid for any nonzero ratio).
A4. Conclusion. Since r > 0, |r⁻¹| = r⁻¹ and |r⁻¹|ⁿ = ofReal(r⁻ⁿ); thus Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = ofReal(r⁻ⁿ) Hⁿ(S). ∎

Part B (lower density; accepted theorem doragm_approxTangent_lower_density; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3), lines 91–95). Let n ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary, x ∈ ℝ^P, and let Q be the approximate tangent space of M at x. Then for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < ωₙ there is ρ₀ > 0 such that c ρⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for all 0 < ρ < ρ₀.
B1. Room. ωₙ < ∞ (a ball has finite Lebesgue measure), so c < ∞. The map s ↦ c(1+s)ⁿ is continuous at s = 0 with value c < ωₙ, so there is s > 0 with c(1+s)ⁿ < ωₙ. Put A := 1 + s.
B2. Test function. ψ(y) := max(0, min(1, (A − |y|)/s)) is continuous with values in [0, 1], ψ = 1 on B̄₁(0) and ψ = 0 outside B̄_A(0); it has compact support, so ψ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).
B3. Mass on the plane. dim Q = n (first conjunct of the definition). An orthonormal basis of Q indexed by {1,…,n} gives a linear isometry j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with range Q and j(B₁(0)) = Q ∩ B₁(0). Hⁿ is invariant under isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`), so Hⁿ(Q ∩ B₁(0)) = ωₙ. Hⁿ⌞Q is finite on compact sets (SimonGMT `regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule`), so ψ is Hⁿ⌞Q-integrable and ∫_Q ψ dHⁿ ≥ ∫_{Q∩B₁(0)} 1 dHⁿ = ωₙ > c Aⁿ.
B4. Convergence. By the definition of approximate tangent space, a(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} ψ dHⁿ → ∫_Q ψ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x). Hence a(r) > c Aⁿ for all sufficiently small r > 0.
B5. Comparison. For r > 0, since 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1_{B̄_A(0)}: ofReal(a(r)) ≤ ∫ ofReal(ψ) d(Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M)) ≤ Hⁿ(B̄_A(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(M)). Moreover B̄_A(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(M) = η_{x,r}(M ∩ B̄_{rA}(x)), and η_{x,r} is the translation y ↦ y − x (an isometry) followed by the homothety of ratio r⁻¹, so by Part A its Hⁿ-measure is r⁻ⁿ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{rA}(x)) (Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image`).
B6. Conclusion. For all small r > 0: c Aⁿ ≤ r⁻ⁿ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{rA}(x)), i.e. c (rA)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{rA}(x)). Since ρ ↦ ρ/A maps a right neighbourhood of 0 into a right neighbourhood of 0, substituting ρ = rA gives c ρⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0. (The hypothesis n ≥ 1 is not needed.) ∎

Part C (vanishing cone density; accepted theorem cbrr_tangent_cone_density_zero; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3), lines 96–107, and formula (6), line 184). Let n ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(M) < ∞, x ∈ ℝ^P, and let Q be the approximate tangent space of M at x; X(x) := {z : 2|p_Q(z − x)| < |z − x|} (Simon's cone X_{1/2}(Q^⊥, x) in the form (2), since dist(v, Q^⊥) = |p_Q v|). Then for every t ∈ (0, ∞] there is ρ₀ > 0 such that Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ t ρⁿ for all 0 < ρ < ρ₀. In C2–C5, X := {y : 2|p_Q y| < |y|} is the cone at 0, so X(x) = x + X.
C0. If t = ∞ the claim is trivial, because ρⁿ > 0 for ρ > 0 makes the right side ∞. Assume 0 < t < ∞.
C1. Smallness on the plane. dim Q = n. An orthonormal basis of Q gives a linear isometry j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with range Q, and j(B̄_r(0)) = Q ∩ B̄_r(0). Since Hⁿ is isometry invariant and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_r(0)) = Lⁿ(B̄_r(0)) = rⁿ ωₙ for r > 0, where ωₙ = Lⁿ(B₁(0)) < ∞ (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`, `Measure.addHaar_closedBall`; ℝⁿ is nontrivial as n ≥ 1). As n ≥ 1, rⁿωₙ → 0 when r → 0; fix s > 0 with Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_{4s}(0)) < t.
C2. Test function. Let h(y) := (3/4)|y| − |p_Q y|, φ(y) := max(0, min(1, 1 + h(y)/s)), χ(y) := max(0, min(1, 2 − |y|)) and f := φ·χ. Then f is continuous, 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, and f = 0 outside B̄₂(0); so f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).
 (a) f = 1 on X ∩ B₁(0): if 2|p_Q y| < |y| and |y| < 1 then h(y) > (3/4)|y| − |y|/2 = |y|/4 ≥ 0, so φ(y) = 1, and χ(y) = 1 because |y| ≤ 1.
 (b) On Q, f vanishes outside B̄_{4s}(0): for y ∈ Q we have p_Q y = y, so h(y) = −|y|/4 and 1 + h(y)/s = 1 − |y|/(4s) < 0 when |y| > 4s, whence φ(y) = 0.
C3. The limit is small. Hⁿ⌞Q is finite on compact sets (SimonGMT `regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule`), so f is Hⁿ⌞Q-integrable and L := ∫_Q f dHⁿ ≥ 0 satisfies ofReal(L) = ∫ ofReal(f) d(Hⁿ⌞Q) ≤ ∫ 1_{B̄_{4s}(0)} d(Hⁿ⌞Q) = Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_{4s}(0)) < t by (b) and f ≤ 1; hence L < t (as real numbers, t < ∞). By the definition of approximate tangent space, I(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → L as r ↓ 0, so I(r) < t for all sufficiently small r > 0.
C4. Comparison for fixed r > 0. By the scaling lemma (Part A), Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(M)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ(M) < ∞, so Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M) is a finite measure, the bounded continuous compactly supported f is integrable for it, and since f ≥ 0, ofReal(I(r)) = ∫ ofReal(f) d(Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M)). By (a), 1_{X∩B₁(0)} ≤ ofReal∘f, and X ∩ B₁(0) is open, so Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(M) ∩ X ∩ B₁(0)) = (Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M))(X ∩ B₁(0)) ≤ ofReal(I(r)).
C5. Rescaling the set. For z ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0: η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x), |p_Q(η_{x,r}(z))| = r⁻¹|p_Q(z − x)| and |η_{x,r}(z)| = r⁻¹|z − x|; hence η_{x,r}(z) ∈ X ⇔ 2|p_Q(z − x)| < |z − x| ⇔ z ∈ X(x), and η_{x,r}(z) ∈ B₁(0) ⇔ |z − x| < r. Therefore η_{x,r}(M) ∩ X ∩ B₁(0) = η_{x,r}(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)), and by Part A its Hⁿ-measure equals ofReal(r⁻ⁿ) Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)).
C6. Conclusion. For all sufficiently small r > 0, C3–C5 give ofReal(r⁻ⁿ) Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ ofReal(I(r)) ≤ t. Multiplying by ofReal(rⁿ) (and ofReal(rⁿ)·ofReal(r⁻ⁿ) = 1) yields Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ t·rⁿ, which is the claim with ρ = r. ∎

Part D (Lusin's theorem; accepted theorem dor_ims_lusin_measurable_continuousOn; Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17). Let Y be a second-countable topological space with a σ-algebra containing the open sets, μ a measure on ℝ^P, A ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with μ(A) < ∞, g : ℝ^P → Y measurable and ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a compact K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε such that g restricted to K is continuous.
D0. If ε = ∞, K := ∅ works because μ(A) < ∞. Assume ε < ∞, so ε is a positive real number.
D1. Inner regularity. ν := μ⌞A is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, which is σ-compact and locally compact, so ν is regular (Mathlib `Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure`); hence every Borel set S has compact subsets C with ν(S ∖ C) arbitrarily small. For C ⊆ A, ν(S ∖ C) = μ((S ∖ C) ∩ A).
D2. Approximating the preimages of a countable base. Let (U_m)_{m∈ℕ} be a countable base of Y (repeat sets if it is finite). For each m, B_m := A ∩ g⁻¹(U_m) and A ∖ B_m are Borel (g is measurable and U_m is open, hence measurable). By D1 choose compact K_m ⊆ B_m and K'_m ⊆ A ∖ B_m with μ(B_m ∖ K_m) < ε/2^{m+3} and μ((A ∖ B_m) ∖ K'_m) < ε/2^{m+3}; then μ(A ∖ (K_m ∪ K'_m)) < ε/2^{m+2}. Also choose a compact K₀ ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K₀) < ε/2.
D3. The compact set. K := K₀ ∩ ⋂_m (K_m ∪ K'_m) is a closed subset of the compact set K₀ (compact sets are closed in ℝ^P), hence compact, and K ⊆ A. Since A ∖ K ⊆ (A ∖ K₀) ∪ ⋃_m (A ∖ (K_m ∪ K'_m)), countable subadditivity gives μ(A ∖ K) < ε/2 + Σ_m ε/2^{m+2} = ε/2 + ε/2 = ε (the first inequality is strict).
D4. Continuity of g on K. Let x ∈ K and let V ⊆ Y be open with g(x) ∈ V; choose m with g(x) ∈ U_m ⊆ V. Then x ∈ B_m, so x ∉ K'_m ⊆ A ∖ B_m, and since x ∈ K_m ∪ K'_m we get x ∈ K_m. The set W := ℝ^P ∖ K'_m is open, contains x, and W ∩ K ⊆ K_m ⊆ B_m ⊆ g⁻¹(V). Hence g maps the relative neighbourhood W ∩ K of x into V, i.e. g|_K is continuous at x. ∎

Part E (main proof; accepted proof of cbrr_uniform_density_on_large_set). Throughout μ := Hⁿ⌞M is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P (Hⁿ(M) < ∞), and for every S ⊆ M we have μ(S) = Hⁿ(S ∩ M) = Hⁿ(S) (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_apply'`, M Borel).
E1. A Borel set of good points. Since x ↦ p_{Q(x)} is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, there is a strongly measurable (Borel) g : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P) with g(x) = p_{Q(x)} for μ-a.e. x. Hence the set Z of points x ∈ M at which g(x) ≠ p_{Q(x)} or M has no approximate tangent space Q(x) at x is μ-null, so Hⁿ(Z) = μ(Z) = 0. Choose a Borel set N ⊇ Z with Hⁿ(N) = 0 (Mathlib `exists_measurable_superset_of_null`) and put M₁ := M ∖ N. Then M₁ is Borel, Hⁿ(M ∖ M₁) = 0, and every x ∈ M₁ satisfies g(x) = p_{Q(x)} and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q(x); in particular dim Q(x) = n.
E2. Lusin: continuity of the plane field on a large closed set (the closed set F of Simon's (4)). L(ℝ^P) is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence second countable, and carries its Borel σ-algebra; g is measurable (being strongly measurable). Apply Part D (Lusin's theorem) to the measure μ, the Borel set A := M₁ (μ(M₁) < ∞), the map g : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P) and the tolerance ofReal(ε/3) ≠ 0: there is a compact K ⊆ M₁ with μ(M₁ ∖ K) < ε/3 on which g is continuous. Put F := K; F is compact, hence closed, F ⊆ M₁ and μ(M₁ ∖ F) < ε/3. Since g(x) = p_{Q(x)} for x ∈ F ⊆ M₁, the map x ↦ p_{Q(x)} is continuous on F in the operator norm.
E3. Pointwise eventual bounds ((5), (6), (7) of the source). Let x ∈ F. By the lower density lemma (Part B, applied with c := ofReal(a) < ωₙ, n ≥ 1) there is ρ₁(x) > 0 with ofReal(a)·ofReal(ρⁿ) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for 0 < ρ < ρ₁(x). By the cone density lemma (Part C, applied with t := ofReal(b) > 0, using n ≥ 1 and Hⁿ(M) < ∞) there is ρ₂(x) > 0 with Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(b)·ofReal(ρⁿ) for 0 < ρ < ρ₂(x). Now ofReal(a)ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(aρⁿ) if a ≥ 0, while ofReal(aρⁿ) = 0 if a < 0, and ofReal(b)ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(bρⁿ). Since Hⁿ(M ∩ S) = μ(S) for Borel S, we get, for 0 < ρ < min(ρ₁(x), ρ₂(x)): ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ).
E4. The sets of uniformity (the source's f_k, q_k). For k ∈ ℕ put δ_k := 1/(k + 1) and
  A_k := {y ∈ ℝ^P : ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)},
  C_k := {x ∈ F : μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ) for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)},
  G_k := A_k ∩ C_k ⊆ F.
 (i) A_k is closed. Fix ρ > 0, s ∈ [0, ∞) and let y_i → y with μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)) ≥ s for all i. If z ∉ B̄_ρ(y) then |z − y| > ρ, so |z − y_i| > ρ for all large i; thus the indicator of U := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y) is ≤ liminf_i of the indicators of U_i := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y_i) (Borel sets), and Fatou's lemma gives μ(U) ≤ liminf_i μ(U_i) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s. As μ is finite, μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(U) ≥ s. So {y : μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≥ s} is sequentially closed, hence closed, and A_k is an intersection of such sets.
 (ii) C_k is closed. Fix ρ > 0, s ∈ [0, ∞) and let x_i ∈ F, x_i → x, with μ(X(x_i) ∩ B_ρ(x_i)) ≤ s. Then x ∈ F because F is closed. Let z ∈ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x). By E2, ‖p_{Q(x_i)} − p_{Q(x)}‖ → 0, hence |p_{Q(x_i)}(z − x_i) − p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| ≤ ‖p_{Q(x_i)} − p_{Q(x)}‖|z − x_i| + |x − x_i| → 0, while |z − x_i| → |z − x|; so the strict inequalities 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x| and |z − x| < ρ persist with x_i in place of x for all large i. Thus 1_{X(x)∩B_ρ(x)} ≤ liminf_i 1_{X(x_i)∩B_ρ(x_i)} pointwise; these sets are open (as X(x_i) is the preimage of an open set under a continuous map), and Fatou's lemma (Mathlib `lintegral_liminf_le`) gives μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ liminf_i μ(X(x_i) ∩ B_ρ(x_i)) ≤ s. So {x ∈ F : μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ s} is sequentially closed, hence closed, and C_k is an intersection of such sets.
 (iii) G_k ⊆ G_{k+1}, since δ_{k+1} < δ_k makes the defining conditions weaker, and ⋃_k G_k = F: for x ∈ F choose k with δ_k ≤ min(ρ₁(x), ρ₂(x)) and use E3.
E5. Egoroff step ((8) of the source). The closed (hence Borel) sets G_k increase to F, so μ(G_k) → μ(F) (Mathlib `tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop`) and, μ being finite and G_k ⊆ F, μ(F ∖ G_k) = μ(F) − μ(G_k) → 0. Fix k with μ(F ∖ G_k) < ε/3 and set E := G_k, δ := δ_k > 0.
E6. Verification ((9) of the source). E ⊆ F ⊆ M₁ ⊆ M. Every x ∈ E lies in M₁, so dim Q(x) = n. For y ∈ E ⊆ A_k and 0 < ρ < δ: ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)). For x ∈ E ⊆ C_k and 0 < ρ < δ: μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ). Finally M ∖ E ⊆ (M ∖ M₁) ∪ (M₁ ∖ F) ∪ (F ∖ E), all three subsets of M, so by subadditivity Hⁿ(M ∖ E) ≤ 0 + μ(M₁ ∖ F) + μ(F ∖ E) < ε/3 + ε/3 < ε. ∎
(Remark: Simon also intersects E with a large ball to make it compact; this is not needed here because the covering step (the accepted theorem cbrr_rectifiable_of_uniform_density, a sibling child of this split) uses countably many balls.)
proof_key_steps: Parts A–D: Hⁿ scales by r⁻ⁿ under η_{x,r}; at a tangent point c ρⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for c < ωₙ and Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) = o(ρⁿ); Lusin's theorem for measurable maps into second-countable spaces.
Replace p_{Q(·)} by a Borel representative g and discard a Borel null set: M₁ ⊆ M of full measure, all points tangent with g = p_{Q(·)}.
Lusin (Part D) on g : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P): compact F ⊆ M₁ with μ(M₁ ∖ F) < ε/3 and x ↦ p_{Q(x)} continuous on F.
At each x ∈ F Parts B and C give the bounds for 0 < ρ < ρ(x).
A_k (closed balls, upper semicontinuity via Fatou on complements) and C_k (open cones, continuity on F + Fatou) are closed; G_k = A_k ∩ C_k increase to F.
Continuity from below: μ(F ∖ G_k) < ε/3 for some k; E := G_k, δ := 1/(k+1) satisfy all conclusions.

subproblems.title: Uniform density and cone bounds imply countable n-rectifiability (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 ⇐: net, (10), Lipschitz graphs)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, E ⊆ ℝ^P, Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces and a, b, δ real with a > 0, b·16ⁿ < a and δ > 0. Assume dim Q(x) = n for x ∈ E, ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) for all y ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ, and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ) for all x ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ, where X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|}. Then E is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable n E).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (E : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a b δ : ℝ), 0 < a → b * 16 ^ n < a → 0 < δ → (∀ x ∈ E, Module.finrank ℝ (Q x) = n) → (∀ y ∈ E, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → ENNReal.ofReal (a * ρ ^ n) ≤ μ (closedBall y ρ)) → (∀ x ∈ E, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → μ ({z | 2 * ‖(Q x).starProjection (z - x)‖ < ‖z - x‖} ∩ ball x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (b * ρ ^ n)) → CountablyRectifiable n E
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cbrr_rectifiable_of_uniform_density (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.rectifiable-a1.uniform_to_rectifiable-a1, status accepted, candidate 15d1af75effb8b2ec1095347205aa50d0f23f911), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. It is steps 4–5 of the selected node's supplied proof (net of planes, the cone claim with the corrected constant, Lipschitz graphs, covering). Part D below reproduces the node's accepted natural-language proof (its frozen handoff text) step by step: the sibling references are renamed to part labels, the steps are relabeled D1–D7 with Simon line citations, and its source paragraph is condensed into the Source line and the Part D header. It cites three accepted DAG theorems at byte-identical frozen types, which are this node's own resolved dependencies: cbrr_projection_net (Part A), cbrr_cone_claim (Part B) and cbrr_lipschitz_cover_of_cone_condition (Part C). The accepted Lean candidate applies exactly these three, and GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean at the candidate commit contains their kernel-checked proofs. So that this proof is self-contained, Parts A–C reproduce the accepted handoff proofs of those three theorems step by step; their source paragraphs are condensed into the part headers and the Dictionary.
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇐", chapter-03.txt lines 220–262 (net of planes, claim (10), Lipschitz graphs via the extension theorem, the cover of E). The iteration over M (lines 263–274) belongs to the parent assembly. Documented erratum: the printed choice ε = 1/16ⁿ (lines 227 and 249) yields only 1 − ε < 16ⁿε = 1 in the proof of (10), which is no contradiction. The corrected ε = 2⁻¹16⁻ⁿ gives 16ⁿε = 1/2 < 1 − ε. It appears here as the hypothesis b·16ⁿ < a, with a = (1 − ε)ωₙ and b = εωₙ in the application.
Dictionary with Simon's notation: for an n-dimensional subspace T put π := T^⊥ (an ℓ-plane, ℓ = P − n). Then |p_T v| = dist(v, π) and ‖p_T − p_{T'}‖ = ‖p_{T^⊥} − p_{T'^⊥}‖ = d(π, π') (Simon (3)). X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|} is Simon's cone X_{1/2}(π_x, x) of (2) with π_x = Q(x)^⊥, taken with strict inequality.

Part A (net of planes; accepted theorem cbrr_projection_net; Simon lines 220–226). For all P, n ∈ ℕ and ε > 0 there are N ∈ ℕ and n-dimensional linear subspaces T₁,…,T_N of ℝ^P such that every n-dimensional linear subspace Q of ℝ^P satisfies ‖p_Q − p_{T_j}‖ < ε for some j (operator norm).
A1. Let S := {p_Q : Q an n-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P} ⊆ L(ℝ^P), the finite-dimensional normed space of linear maps with the operator norm.
A2. Every orthogonal projection has norm ≤ 1 (Mathlib `Submodule.starProjection_norm_le`), so S ⊆ B̄₁(0).
A3. L(ℝ^P) is finite-dimensional, hence proper; so B̄₁(0) is compact, hence totally bounded, and so is its subset S.
A4. By total boundedness there is a finite set t ⊆ S with S ⊆ ⋃_{L∈t} B_ε(L) (Mathlib `finite_approx_of_totallyBounded`).
A5. Every L ∈ t equals p_{T_L} for some n-dimensional subspace T_L (choose one). Enumerate t as L₁,…,L_N and put T_j := T_{L_j}; each T_j is n-dimensional.
A6. If Q is n-dimensional then p_Q ∈ S, so ‖p_Q − L_j‖ < ε for some j, i.e. ‖p_Q − p_{T_j}‖ < ε. (If ℝ^P has no n-dimensional subspace, S = t = ∅ and N = 0 works vacuously.) ∎

Part B (claim (10); accepted theorem cbrr_cone_claim; Simon lines 227–249 with the corrected constant). Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, E ⊆ ℝ^P, Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces, T a linear subspace and a, b, δ real numbers with a > 0 and b·16ⁿ < a. Assume ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) for all y ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ, and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ) for all x ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ. Then for all x, y ∈ E with ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_T‖ < 1/16 and |y − x| < δ/2 we have |y − x| ≤ 4|p_T(y − x)|.
B1. Suppose the conclusion fails: σ := |y − x| satisfies 4|p_T(y − x)| < σ. Then σ > 0, and σ < δ/2 by hypothesis.
B2. B̄_{σ/8}(y) ⊆ X(x) ∩ B_{2σ}(x). Let |z − y| ≤ σ/8. Since z − x = (y − x) + (z − y) and ‖p_{Q(x)}‖ ≤ 1,
  |p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| ≤ |p_{Q(x)}(y − x)| + |z − y| ≤ |p_T(y − x)| + ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_T‖·σ + σ/8 < σ/4 + σ/16 + σ/8 = 7σ/16,
 using |p_T(y − x)| < σ/4 and ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_T‖σ < σ/16. Also |z − x| ≥ |y − x| − |z − y| ≥ 7σ/8 and |z − x| ≤ |y − x| + |z − y| ≤ 9σ/8 < 2σ. Hence 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < 7σ/8 ≤ |z − x|, i.e. z ∈ X(x), and z ∈ B_{2σ}(x).
B3. Since 0 < σ/8 < δ and 0 < 2σ < δ, the hypotheses (with y and with x, both in E) and monotonicity of μ give ofReal(a(σ/8)ⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_{σ/8}(y)) ≤ μ(X(x) ∩ B_{2σ}(x)) ≤ ofReal(b(2σ)ⁿ).
B4. As a(σ/8)ⁿ > 0, the inequality between the ofReal values forces a(σ/8)ⁿ ≤ b(2σ)ⁿ = b·16ⁿ·(σ/8)ⁿ; dividing by (σ/8)ⁿ > 0 gives a ≤ b·16ⁿ, contradicting b·16ⁿ < a. Hence |y − x| ≤ 4|p_T(y − x)|. ∎

Part C (Lipschitz parametrization; accepted theorem cbrr_lipschitz_cover_of_cone_condition; Simon lines 249–257 with the extension theorem 1.2 of Ch. 2). Let T be a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim T = n, D ⊆ ℝ^P and C ∈ ℝ such that |y − x| ≤ C|p_T(y − x)| for all x, y ∈ D. Then there is a Lipschitz map F : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with D ⊆ F(ℝⁿ). (D is parametrized directly over ℝⁿ ≅ T, which is the composition of Simon's graph map with his orthogonal transformation.)
C1. Let C' := max(C, 0) ≥ 0. Since |p_T(·)| ≥ 0, |y − x| ≤ C'|p_T(y − x)| for x, y ∈ D.
C2. A linear chart of T. As dim T = n, an orthonormal basis of T indexed by {1,…,n} gives a linear isometry ι : T → ℝⁿ. Let L := ι ∘ (orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto T) : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ. L is linear and |Lv − Lw| = |p_T(v − w)| for all v, w.
C3. Inverse on L(D). For x, y ∈ D, |y − x| ≤ C'|Ly − Lx|; in particular L is injective on D. Define g : L(D) → ℝ^P by g(Lx) := x. Then |g(u) − g(v)| ≤ C'|u − v| for u, v ∈ L(D), i.e. g is C'-Lipschitz on L(D).
C4. McShane extension coordinatewise. Identify ℝ^P with (Fin P → ℝ) carrying the sup norm; the identification is 1-Lipschitz (|v|_∞ ≤ |v|), so the coordinate map of g is C'-Lipschitz on L(D). By McShane's extension theorem applied to each coordinate (Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi`, built on `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`) there is a C'-Lipschitz G : ℝⁿ → (Fin P → ℝ) that agrees with the coordinates of g on L(D).
C5. Back to the Euclidean norm. The map (Fin P → ℝ) → ℝ^P, v ↦ v, is √P-Lipschitz from the sup norm to the Euclidean norm (|v| ≤ √P|v|_∞; Mathlib `PiLp.antilipschitzWith_ofLp`). Hence F := (this map) ∘ G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is Lipschitz with constant √P·C'.
C6. Covering. For x ∈ D, F(Lx) = g(Lx) = x, so D ⊆ F(ℝⁿ). ∎

Part D (main proof; accepted proof of cbrr_rectifiable_of_uniform_density). Simon covers the compact set E by finitely many balls B_{δ/4}(x₀). Since only countable rectifiability is required, we cover ℝ^P by countably many such balls with centres in a dense sequence, so E need not be compact.
D1. Net of planes (Simon lines 220–226). By Part A with ε := 1/16 there are n-dimensional subspaces T₁,…,T_N such that every n-dimensional Q has some j with ‖p_Q − p_{T_j}‖ < 1/16.
D2. Dense centres. ℝ^P is separable; fix a sequence (u_q)_{q∈ℕ} with dense range.
D3. Pieces. For j ∈ {1,…,N} and q ∈ ℕ put D_{j,q} := {x ∈ E : ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_{T_j}‖ < 1/16} ∩ B_{δ/4}(u_q).
D4. Cone condition on each piece (claim (10)). Let x, y ∈ D_{j,q}. Then |y − x| ≤ |y − u_q| + |x − u_q| < δ/4 + δ/4 = δ/2, x ∈ E with ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_{T_j}‖ < 1/16 and y ∈ E. Part B (applied to μ, E, Q, T := T_j, a, b, δ and the two density hypotheses) gives |y − x| ≤ 4|p_{T_j}(y − x)|.
D5. Lipschitz parametrization (Simon lines 249–257). Since dim T_j = n, Part C (with T := T_j, D := D_{j,q}, C := 4) gives a Lipschitz F_{j,q} : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with D_{j,q} ⊆ F_{j,q}(ℝⁿ).
D6. The pieces cover E (Simon lines 258–262). Let x ∈ E. As dim Q(x) = n, D1 gives j with ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_{T_j}‖ < 1/16; by density there is q with |x − u_q| < δ/4. Hence x ∈ D_{j,q}. So E ⊆ ⋃_{(j,q)} F_{j,q}(ℝⁿ), the union over the countable index set {1,…,N} × ℕ.
D7. Conclusion. Each F_{j,q}(ℝⁿ) is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_range`); the family {F_{j,q}(ℝⁿ)} is countable, so its union is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_sUnion`), and so is its subset E (SimonGMT `CountablyRectifiable.mono`). ∎
